argument: Primary challenge is data staleness, and it is decisive. The proposal quotes ISRG 365.73 and an entry ratio of 10.29, but the verified Friday 2026-08-07 15:59 ET close (prices.py, yfinance feed) is ISRG 378.71 (+1.34% on the day) vs RSPH 35.54 (+1.17%) — a pair ratio of ~10.66. That is 3.6% above the proposed entry and within ~0.8% of the stated stop at 10.75. The proposal's own number-one risk — 'violent short-covering bounce toward 11+' — appears to already be in progress: ISRG outperformed its hedge leg on Friday and the ratio has reclaimed roughly half the distance to the stop before the position even exists. Entering Monday at ~10.66 with a 10.75 stop is not a trade with a 4.4% stop buffer; it is a trade with sub-1% room to an immediate stop-out, which guts the stated risk math (target_ratio 9.55 vs stop 10.75 implies ~7.2% reward vs ~4.5% risk from 10.29 — from 10.66 it is ~10.4% reward vs ~0.8% risk, a completely different bet than the one pitched). If this trade is to live, it needs re-struck levels off the Friday print and an honest answer to whether the 10.7-11.0 reclaim zone the proposal itself flagged as the distribution-confirmation level is being tested from below right now. Secondary macro points from my seat, offered with the caveat that a US medtech pair carries minimal CEEMEA factor content and my informational edge here is thin: (1) the dollar is softening — UUP -0.46% Friday — and ISRG carries roughly a third of revenue ex-US, so USD translation is a mild tailwind to the short's target, not a headwind to the name; (2) TLT +0.28% Friday — if the rates backdrop is easing, long-duration premium-multiple medtech is exactly the bucket that catches a duration bid, working against the multiple-compression thesis at the margin. Neither macro point is strong enough to kill the idea; the stale entry geometry is. Recommendation to PM: do not fill at Monday's open off the 365.73/10.29 framing — require the originator to restate entry, stop, and target off the 2026-08-07 close and re-confirm the trend signal hasn't been invalidated by Friday's ISRG outperformance.
